title: Safe parking sites for people living in cars
summary: A county safe parking pilot on private land at 21 Hanson Road stalled after flooding, with no project money spent, and staff began looking at county land instead. A council resolution urging a managed safe parking project failed 4–2. Bill 133 would loosen hours and license rules so the county can open a temporary 24-hour site, with a shuttle, for unsheltered people being relocated.

timeline.text: A County director said the temporary site will run 24 hours, with a shuttle to the transit hub.
A County director said staff will help safe parking participants get an ID or driver's license.
A County attorney said sites under the ordinance would have to be county controlled in some form.
Acting on the bill lets the County move ahead with a temporary safe parking site for unsheltered people being relocated.
The bill removes driver's license, vehicle registration, and safety check requirements that some participants may lack.
Bill 133 would allow more flexibility in the hours and conditions of each safe parking site.
The resolution failed with four ayes and two noes.
Resolution 26-150 urged the administration to carry out a managed safe overnight parking project.
